title: Hike below the rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Going down is optional, coming back up is not - rangers pull people off the Bright Angel Trail every summer. Go in spring or autumn.

title: Reach the quieter North Rim of the Grand Canyon
description: Takes about a tenth of the visitors, sits 300m higher, and closes under snow from December. Four hours' drive from the South Rim to go 16km.

title: Raft the Colorado through the Grand Canyon
description: Up to three weeks and 440km through the canyon floor. Private permits run on a weighted lottery with a wait that has run to years.

title: Walk down to Havasu Falls
description: Turquoise water from travertine minerals, 16km down into Havasupai land. Permits sell out within minutes on the February release and are non-transferable.

title: See the light beams in Antelope Canyon
description: A slot canyon on Navajo Nation land, accessible only with a Navajo guide. The shafts of light appear around midday from about March to October.

title: Stand above Horseshoe Bend
description: A 270-degree meander of the Colorado, 300m below an unfenced sandstone rim. Twenty minutes from the car park, and no shade at all.

title: Drive the valley floor at Monument Valley
description: A Navajo tribal park, not a national park - the sandstone buttes John Ford filmed nine times. The 27km loop road is rough but doable in a normal car.

title: Win the lottery for The Wave at Coyote Buttes
description: Undulating Navajo sandstone laid down as dunes 190 million years ago. Only 64 people a day get in, by lottery, and the route is unmarked.

title: Climb Cathedral Rock at sunset in Sedona
description: Iron-stained sandstone spires, a serious short scramble, and a town built around the belief that the rocks emit energy vortexes.

title: Walk among the saguaro at sunset
description: Saguaro grow only in the Sonoran, take 35 years to flower and 75 to sprout an arm. The tallest here are over 12m.

title: See the fossil logs at Petrified Forest
description: 225-million-year-old trees turned to quartz, plus a stretch of original Route 66. One of the very few national parks where dogs can join you on trails.

title: Drive the surviving stretches of Route 66
description: Decommissioned in 1985 and replaced by interstates, but long segments survive as business routes through towns the freeway bypassed.

title: Look into Meteor Crater
description: 1.2km wide and 170m deep, punched out 50,000 years ago and the first crater on earth proven to be from an impact. Apollo crews trained in it.

title: Wade The Narrows in Zion
description: Walking up the Virgin River between 300m walls that close to nine metres apart. Closed whenever flash flood risk is high - check daily.

title: Walk the chains up Angels Landing
description: A 500m spine with chains and drops on both sides. Permits have been required since 2022, by lottery, and the fatality count is in the teens.

title: Walk down among the hoodoos at Bryce Canyon
description: Not a canyon but an eroding escarpment holding the densest concentration of hoodoos on earth. The Navajo Loop takes you between them.

title: Walk to Delicate Arch for sunset
description: The arch on Utah's licence plates - 4.8km return over slickrock with no shade. Arches has held over 2,000 arches and loses one occasionally.

title: Watch sunrise through Mesa Arch at Canyonlands
description: For about twenty minutes at dawn the underside of the arch glows orange from light bouncing off the canyon below.

title: Drive the Burr Trail through Capitol Reef
description: A 160km wrinkle in the earth's crust called the Waterpocket Fold, and the least visited of Utah's five parks. Pick fruit in the Fruita orchards in season.

title: Wander the mushroom rocks at Goblin Valley
description: A valley of squat hoodoos you are actually encouraged to scramble over - rare in a landscape this fragile, and excellent for it.

title: Drive on the Bonneville Salt Flats
description: About 120 square kilometres of salt crust where land speed records have been set since 1912. Wet for much of the year - check before driving on.

title: Find Spiral Jetty on the Great Salt Lake
description: Robert Smithson's 460m basalt coil from 1970, submerged for thirty years and now high and dry as the lake shrinks - which is its own commentary.

title: Sled the gypsum dunes at White Sands
description: 275 square miles of white gypsum sand you can toboggan down. Dogs are allowed on leash almost everywhere here, unusually.

title: Watch the bat flight at Carlsbad Caverns
description: Hundreds of thousands of Brazilian free-tailed bats spiral out of the natural entrance at dusk. Walk in through the same hole rather than taking the lift.

title: Climb the ladders to the cliff dwellings at Bandelier
description: Ancestral Pueblo homes carved into volcanic tuff, occupied for four centuries. Wooden ladders take you up into the alcoves themselves.

title: Walk the adobe streets of Santa Fe
description: Founded in 1610 and the oldest capital in the US, with a building code that has kept the whole centre in adobe. Georgia O'Keeffe's museum is here.

title: Visit Taos Pueblo
description: Continuously inhabited for over 1,000 years - the oldest such community in the US, and still without electricity or running water by choice.

title: See the dishes at the Very Large Array
description: 27 radio dishes, each 25m across, moved along rail tracks into different configurations across a high desert plain. Contact was filmed here.

title: Drive Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park
description: The highest continuous paved road in the US, topping 3,713m, with eighteen kilometres above the treeline. Timed entry applies in summer.

title: See the Maroon Bells reflected at dawn
description: Reputedly the most photographed peaks in North America, and lethal to climb - the mudstone is so loose they are known as the Deadly Bells.

title: Sandboard the Great Sand Dunes
description: The tallest dunes in North America at 230m, against the Sangre de Cristo range, with a seasonal creek at their base you can float down in spring.

title: Tour the Cliff Palace at Mesa Verde
description: 150 rooms built into an alcove by Ancestral Puebloans around 1200 CE and abandoned within a century. Ranger-guided entry only, ladders included.

title: Drive the Million Dollar Highway to Ouray
description: 40km of US 550 over three passes with no guardrails and a sheer drop on the outside lane. Built on an 1880s toll road for the silver mines.

title: Look into the Black Canyon of the Gunnison
description: So narrow and deep that parts of the floor get 33 minutes of sunlight a day. The Painted Wall is the tallest cliff in Colorado at 682m.

title: Watch the Grand Prismatic Spring from the overlook
description: The world's first national park, sitting on an active supervolcano. The overlook trail beats the boardwalk for seeing the colours.

title: Watch wolves at dawn in the Lamar Valley
description: Wolves were reintroduced in 1995 after seventy years' absence, and this valley is where you have the best chance. Bring a spotting scope and get up early.

title: Wait for Old Faithful to go off
description: Erupts every 60 to 110 minutes and is predicted to within ten minutes - the most predictable big geyser anywhere, though not the largest.

title: Paddle Jenny Lake under the Tetons
description: The range rises 2,100m straight off the valley floor with no foothills at all, because the fault runs right along its base.

title: Walk the base trail around Devils Tower
description: The first US national monument, declared in 1906. Sacred to more than twenty tribes, who ask climbers to stay off voluntarily through June.

title: Drive the Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier
description: 80km over Logan Pass, only fully open for about ten weeks a year, and now requiring a timed entry reservation in peak season.

title: Walk the Highline Trail along the Garden Wall
description: Cut into a cliff along the Continental Divide, with a hand cable on the exposed opening section and mountain goats using the same path.

title: Walk the lava fields at Craters of the Moon
description: 1,600 square kilometres of basalt flows and lava tubes, last erupted about 2,000 years ago. Apollo astronauts trained here in 1969.

title: See Shoshone Falls at full flow
description: At 65m it is higher than Niagara, but irrigation takes most of the water for much of the year - spring runoff is the only time it performs.

title: Walk to Sawtooth Lake
description: A granite range with over 400 alpine lakes and no road through the middle of it, in one of the largest dark-sky reserves in the country.

title: Walk the Notch Trail in Badlands
description: A wooden ladder up a cliff face leads to a ledge over the White River valley, through eroded sediment laid down 75 million years ago.

title: See the faces at Mount Rushmore
description: Carved 1927-41 into a granite face in the Black Hills - land the Supreme Court ruled in 1980 was taken from the Lakota unlawfully.

title: Drive the Wildlife Loop in Custer State Park
description: A herd of around 1,400 bison, plus the Needles Highway with tunnels cut so tight they have to be measured before you drive them.

title: See the wild horses in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
description: The only national park named for a person, on the ranch land that turned him into a conservationist. Feral horses and bison on the loop road.

title: Walk into Santa Elena Canyon at Big Bend
description: 460m limestone walls with the Rio Grande running between them - the US on one bank, Mexico on the other, close enough to shout across.

title: Watch 1.5 million bats leave Congress Avenue Bridge
description: The largest urban bat colony in the world, roosting in bridge expansion joints and pouring out at dusk from March to October.

title: Queue for brisket in Texas Hill Country
description: Post oak, salt, pepper and about twelve hours. The best places sell out by early afternoon and the queue starts before they open.

title: Walk the River Walk and the Alamo
description: A flood control scheme from the 1930s turned into a river-level promenade, linking to four Spanish missions that are World Heritage listed.

title: Ride into Palo Duro Canyon
description: The second largest canyon in the US, 190km long and up to 240m deep, and almost nobody outside Texas knows it exists.

title: Wait for the Marfa lights
description: Unexplained lights reported since 1883, with a purpose-built viewing area on US 90 - and a town that became a minimalist art destination because Donald Judd moved in.
